Recreate the graph shown below. It shows monthly homicides in Baltimore, with a reference added for the date of the arrest of Freddie Gray and color used to show colder months (November through April) versus warmer months (May through October). There is a smooth line added to help show seasonal and long-term trends in this data.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Loading all libraries needed:
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(scales)
library(purrr)


```



```{r data set up, warning = FALSE}

homicides <- read_csv("data/homicide-data.csv")

homicides <- homicides %>%
  mutate(city_name = paste(city, state, sep = ", "))

head(homicides)

Baltimore <- homicides %>% 
  filter(city_name == "Baltimore, MD") %>%
  mutate(Date = ymd(reported_date)) %>%  
  mutate(Year = year(Date)) %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date)) %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarize(Monthly_homicides = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Winter = Month %in% c(11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4)) %>%
  mutate(Summer = Month %in% c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10)) %>%
  mutate(Season = ifelse(Winter, "Winter", "Summer")) %>%
  mutate(Date = paste(Year, Month, sep = "-"))
  

```


making the graph

```{r graph fig.width = 4.5, fig.height = 8}

Baltimore %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Date, y = Monthly_homicides, fill = Season)) + 
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Summer" = "lightgray", "Winter" = "lightblue")) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Monthly Homicides", title = "Homicides in Baltimore, MD") +
  theme_minimal()


```
